item.title: Greenwave Q2 FY26 net loss narrows 34.09% to $3.24 million; revenue rises 45.47% to $16 million
item.description: Greenwave posted a net loss available to common stockholders of USD 3.24 million, narrowing 34.09% year over year. Revenue rose 45.47% to USD 16 million, dr
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Greenwave posted a net loss available to common stockholders of USD 3.24 million, narrowing 34.09% year over year. Revenue rose 45.47% to USD 16 million, driven by higher metal revenue and lower hauling revenue. Operating loss narrowed 38.8% to USD 2.85 million, despite operating expenses rising 31.66% to USD 8.91 million. Gross profit more than doubled to USD 6.06 million on higher metal margins, partly offset by weaker hauling margins. Cash was USD 654,987 at June 30, 2026; working capital deficit totaled USD 23.05 million, raising going-concern doubt. item.title: OmniQ Q2 FY26 operating loss widens to $2.22 million; revenue falls 5.47% to $7.38 million
item.description: OmniQ posted a net loss of USD 2.43 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026, versus a net loss of USD 34,000. Revenue fell 4.61% to USD 15.06 million
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: OmniQ posted a net loss of USD 2.43 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026, versus a net loss of USD 34,000. Revenue fell 4.61% to USD 15.06 million, with the decline attributed to customer project timing and a stronger Israeli shekel. Operating loss widened to USD 3.49 million as operating expenses climbed 49.98% to USD 7.26 million. Cash totaled USD 1.1 million at June 30, 2026, while the working capital deficit widened to USD 15.2 million. item.title: Lion Copper and Gold held annual general meeting, shareholders voted on proposals
item.description: Lion Copper and Gold held its annual general meeting on Aug. 12, 2026, with shareholders backing a slate of governance measures. Shareholders set the board
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Lion Copper and Gold held its annual general meeting on Aug. 12, 2026, with shareholders backing a slate of governance measures. Shareholders set the board size at five, endorsing the company’s proposed director lineup without detailing further changes. MNP LLP was reappointed as auditor, with director-set remuneration authorized rather than finalized. A 2026 Stock and Incentive Plan was adopted, enabling equity-based awards under the new plan framework. Investors authorized a share consolidation within a 1-for-20 to 1-for-30 range, leaving ratio and timing to the board. Articles were amended to raise the shareholder-meeting quorum to two or more holders representing at least 33 1/3% of voting shares. item.title: Chile economy misses forecasts as mining slump drags GDP lower
item.description: Chile’s economy posted an annual decline in the second quarter, according to official data published on Tuesday, missing expectations as lower copper produ
item.dc:creator: Mining.com
item.content:encoded: Chile’s economy posted an annual decline in the second quarter, according to official data published on Tuesday, missing expectations as lower copper production hit its key mining sector. The Andean nation’s economy contracted 0.2% in the period from a year earlier, central bank data showed. Despite improving slightly from a revised 0.3% year-on-year contraction in the first quarter, gross domestic product missed economists’ forecasts of 0.1% growth. According to the central bank, the economic activity of the world’s largest copper producer was hampered by the key mining sector that decreased 6.4% due to lower production of the red metal. “Copper mining operations were affected by lower ore grades and maintenance work that reduced production at the country’s major deposits,” the central bank detailed in a report. “The surprisingly poor Q2 GDP outturn in Chile, coming alongside the recent fall in inflation, will reduce any pressure on the central bank to tighten monetary policy,” Capital Economics analyst Kimberley Sperrfechter said in a note. Chile’s central bank is expected to keep its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 4.5% at its next meeting in September and hold that level for the next 24 months, juggling inflation moderation and economic instability. The Andean country’s economy stood flat in the second quarter from the previous three-month period, missing expectations of 0.3% growth forecast in a Reuters poll. Despite the lack of expansion, the quarter performed better than the previous one, which contracted 0.3%. (Reporting by Aida Pelaez-Fernandez and Carlos Serrano; Editing by Chizu Nomiyama and Alison Williams)

EBITDA excluding IPO costs now seen at DKK -1 million to 0.5 million, down from DKK 0.5 million to 3.8 million. IPO costs expected at about DKK 2.5 million.
